title: The Pioneer Incentive Pool pays the Savings Rate on unrewarded bridged USDS into an account the Pioneer Prime fully retains
content:
A.2.2.9.3.1.3 gives the Pioneer Prime a second benefit: during the Pioneer Phase, "all Unrewarded USDS bridged to the Pioneer Chain counts towards Pioneer Incentive payments." A.2.2.9.3.1.4 defines the payment as, each Monthly Settlement Cycle, "an amount of funds equivalent to the Sky Savings Rate multiplied by the balance of Unrewarded USDS" paid "into a separate account controlled by the Pioneer Prime (the 'Pioneer Incentive Pool'). The Pioneer Prime retains **one hundred percent (100%)** of the funds in the Pioneer Incentive Pool."

The formula is identical to the Integration Boost (A.2.2.9.2.2.1.1) but the intent is opposite. The Boost carries a non-binding expectation of pass-through to partners and end users; the Pioneer Incentive Pool states outright that the Prime keeps everything. The same arithmetic funds a subsidy in one case and a discretionary war chest in the other.

That discretion is presumably the design. Bootstrapping USDS on a new chain requires spending on things no rule can enumerate in advance — liquidity provision, partner deals, local integrations — so the Pioneer is given a budget scaled to adoption and left to allocate it. The pool grows exactly as unrewarded balances on the chain grow, so the Pioneer's spending power tracks its own success.

The segregation into "a separate account" is what makes the arrangement legible: incentive funds are distinguishable from the Prime's other holdings, and the pool's size is an observable measure of how much unrewarded USDS the chain holds.
description: Paid monthly at the Sky Savings Rate times unrewarded USDS balances, with the Pioneer Prime keeping 100% — the same formula as the Integration Boost, but explicitly not a pass-through.
